A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same PAPL research, with readable text, equations, figures, tables and complete appendices. Renumbered and relocated material can be matched reliably.

before.justification: v1 reports original protein, text and code generation experiments in Tables 1–4, together with ablations, training curves and HumanEval case studies.

after.justification: v2 retains those experiments and adds original sampler comparisons, training-loss analysis and numerical evaluation of loss approximations.

M1.justification: Algorithm 1, the PAPL objective in Equation 7, soft planner weighting, gradient detachment and uniform masking remain unchanged. Corrected masking indices agree with v1's existing procedural description. New appendix derivations and sampler instantiations do not establish a changed PAPL training procedure.

E1.justification: Both versions use UniRef50 proteins, OpenWebText, FineCode and the same code completion and infilling benchmarks. The added analyses reuse these domains and tasks; discussion of possible out-of-distribution failures introduces no actual evaluation coverage.

E2.justification: New Table 5 compares P2-Self with Greedy and Probability Margin decoding on text. New Table 6 compares P2-self with Vanilla Ancestral, Greedy Ancestral, Entropy-based Confidence and TopK-Margin on code. These substantially expand evaluated sampler comparisons; the model-level comparator sets in Tables 1–4 remain unchanged.

E3.justification: The original benchmark protocols remain unchanged. Added experiments hold the denoiser fixed while varying samplers. Appendix C.3 introduces whole-trajectory loss accumulation using a batch of 1024 and a protein checkpoint with alpha = 5 and tau = 1. Table 6 leaves its infilling length conditions unclear despite repeating the existing oracle-length scores.

E4.justification: v2 adds controlled sampler ablations in B.2.2 and B.3.2, comparative training-loss dynamics in C.2, and an approximation-stage analysis in C.3. Section 4.4 also reports deterioration above alpha = 5. The earlier pure-loss instability analysis and HumanEval case studies are retained, with the latter moved to C.4.

E5.justification: Neither version reports experimental seed counts, repeated-run uncertainty, confidence intervals or significance tests. The new batch-based loss measurements and qualitative warning about unstable correction terms do not introduce uncertainty quantification.

E6.justification: Tables 1–4 retain their numerical results, but v2 adds substantial sampler rankings and diagnostic results. Table 5 reports T = 128 MAUVE of 0.056 for Greedy, 0.051 for Probability Margin and 0.067 for P2-Self. Table 6 adds code sampler scores, while Table 7 and Figure 6 add approximation-loss values and training dynamics. These are additional findings, not improved versions of the original benchmark scores.

T1.justification: v2 adds an optimal-planner proposition and proof in A.1.5, a formal derivation connecting the surrogate objective to PAPL in A.2.3, and a temperature-dependent loss-ordering result in A.2.4. It also corrects the greedy counterexample, restores a missing logarithm in the greedy ELBO, corrects masking domains, and adds formal sampler instantiations in A.2 and A.5.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction and conclusion retain the central training–inference mismatch claim, generalized P-ELBO, simple PAPL modification and headline protein, text and code improvements. The additional analyses elaborate these contributions without redefining their central scope.

C2.justification: v2 substantially expands interpretations of sampler behavior, confidence-dependent training and approximation losses, and discusses excessive planner weighting and planner-specific post-training costs. Some new interpretations conflict with the evidence: B.2.2 claims Probability Margin does not improve monotonically with more steps, although Table 5 reports MAUVE increasing from 0.011 to 0.039 to 0.051.

D1.justification: The abstract now provides a PAPL repository address and states code is available; v1 only promises release upon publication. Appendix D adds recommended starting values and alpha-tuning guidance, and C.3 documents its checkpoint, batch size and hyperparameters. The original implementation and hardware descriptions are retained.

R1.justification: v2 adds Large Language Diffusion Models and Fast-dLLM references when relating the framework to block denoising and confidence thresholding, and expands discussion of probability-margin sampling. Most other bibliography edits update publication metadata or consolidate duplicate references rather than change research positioning.

P1.justification: The main narrative and section order largely persist. Changes include localized explanatory paragraphs, an expanded conclusion, additional appendix subsections, a practitioner guide, author and affiliation updates, and language corrections. The appendix outline becomes a contents list; existing prose is not extensively rewritten.

P2.justification: Figure 1 is replaced by a new comparison of uniform and planner-weighted trajectories. Figure 6 and Tables 5–7 are added. Existing performance curves, protein visualizations and instability plots are retained, with several figures and tables relocated or renumbered. These constitute substantial changes to the visual presentation.

improvement.justification: Corrected formulas, controlled sampler comparisons, approximation analysis and practical instructions improve the paper's auditability. However, the new optimal-planner proof in A.1.5 does not justify replacing optimization of a planner-dependent path expectation with independent pointwise minimizations. New interpretive claims also contradict Table 5, and Table 6 obscures the oracle-length context of retained infilling scores. These substantive reliability concerns offset clear documentation and analytical gains, preventing a confident net-quality judgment.
